statements.status_notes: CVE-2019-1010220 reports the same print_prefix() over-read in print-hncp.c that is described for CVE-2018-19519. Upstream treats it as a duplicate of that issue (https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/tcpdump/issues/763) and fixed both in commit 511915bef7e4de2f31b8d9f581b4a44b0cfbcf53 (https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/tcpdump/commit/511915bef7e4de2f31b8d9f581b4a44b0cfbcf53). That change is included in upstream tcpdump 4.99.5, the release this package is built from, and the shipped print-hncp.c returns the decode_prefix6() error before printing, so the vulnerable code path is not present in the shipped tcpdump binary. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2019-1010220

CVE-2018-19519 is an over-read of an uninitialized buffer in print_prefix() in print-hncp.c: when decode_prefix6() failed, the function printed the buffer anyway. Upstream fixed this in commit 511915bef7e4de2f31b8d9f581b4a44b0cfbcf53 (https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/tcpdump/commit/511915bef7e4de2f31b8d9f581b4a44b0cfbcf53, upstream issue https://github.com/the-tcpdump-group/tcpdump/issues/763). That change is included in upstream tcpdump 4.99.5, the release this package is built from, and the shipped print-hncp.c returns the decode_prefix6() error before printing. The vulnerable code path is therefore not present in the shipped tcpdump binary. Debian tracks the issue as unfixed for its source package: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-19519
